item.title: Something worth a smile this week… Royal Caribbean has hosted its biggest-ever Seminar at Sea, and nearly 200 agents from the UK and Ireland were on board for it. 🚢
item.description:
Something worth a smile this week… Royal Caribbean has hosted its biggest-ever Seminar at Sea, and nearly 200 agents from the UK and Ireland were on board for it. 🚢
They sailed Legend of the Seas from 16 to 20 August, out of Barcelona to Palma de Mallorca and La Spezia, four nights of hands-on training alongside 350+ partners from across EMEA. It's Royal's first Icon Class ship in Europe, so for a lot of agents this was their first close look at the newest ship afloat.
The days covered the onboard experiences, the suites, the ports and Royal's wider destinations… plus a look at their new AI-powered live translation tool. And yes, the Hollywoodland Supper Club and a Charlie and the Chocolate Factory attraction both made the cut. ✨
When you've walked a ship yourself, you sell it with more confidence. That's the whole point of a week like this.

item.title: One for the Disney fans on your books 🌍
item.description:
One for the Disney fans on your books 🌍
Disney Cruise Line is sailing back to New York after a four-year break, and the Disney Wish is the ship making the return.
A New York departure is a lovely fly-cruise to build for UK clients ✈️ transatlantic flight, a few days in the city, then the sailing itself. Seven voyages run from autumn 2027 into spring 2028, once she has finished her first European season.
Two head up to New England and Atlantic Canada, calling at Boston, Saint John and Halifax. One sails to San Juan, and the rest reposition down to Port Canaveral by way of The Bahamas.
Here is the date to hold onto 💡 Castaway Club members can book from 31 August 2026, and general booking opens to everyone on 8 September 2026.
So if you have Disney-loyal families on your books, a little heads-up now means they are ready the moment booking opens.

item.title: Heading through Barcelona with clients over the next few weeks? Worth a quick read. ✈️
item.description:
Heading through Barcelona with clients over the next few weeks? Worth a quick read. ✈️
Groundforce ground-handling staff at Barcelona-El Prat have been on an indefinite strike since 4 August, and according to Breaking Travel News it could run into September. Check-in and baggage handling are the services affected, so holidaymakers are being told to prepare for possible flight and baggage delays.
Here is the bit that matters for a departure day. 💡 When bag drop and check-in slow down, it is all about timing. A slow queue eats the buffer, and anyone with a tight onward connection, a booked transfer, or a cruise to meet feels it first.
That is where an agent earns their keep. A client who booked alone is refreshing news sites at midnight, in the same phone queue as everyone else. A client who booked with you has someone in their corner, ready to talk to the airline the moment anything moves.
A quick heads-up to anyone Barcelona-bound goes a long way… pack essentials in hand luggage, keep airline updates switched on, and leave room around tight connections.

item.title: Something a bit different is happening on UK and Irish shores this fortnight 🌍
item.description:
Something a bit different is happening on UK and Irish shores this fortnight 🌍
SeaDream Yacht Club is bringing SeaDream II into home waters for the first time, and it's inviting agents aboard while it's here.
Nine yacht visits are running from 29 August to 8 September, calling at Glasgow, Belfast, Dublin, the Isle of Man, Workington and Fowey. Nearly 100 agents are expected to step on board, which makes it the line's biggest regional agent programme yet.
For anyone near one of those ports, it's a genuine chance to see a small luxury yacht up close, walk the decks, and get a real feel for who this style of holiday suits… no flight required.
Most visits are already full, mind you, so if you miss out this time, it's one to keep on your radar. A programme this size rarely stays a one-off 😎

item.title: Bit of winter reshuffling from MSC Cruises this week, and it's one to know about if you've got clients holding cruise plans for late 2027 into 2028. 🚢
item.description:
Bit of winter reshuffling from MSC Cruises this week, and it's one to know about if you've got clients holding cruise plans for late 2027 into 2028. 🚢
MSC World Europa's planned Middle East deployment for that winter has been pulled. Instead, the ship sails 7-night western Med itineraries from Barcelona, Genoa, Civitavecchia, Messina, Valletta and Marseille.
There's more movement too … MSC World Asia heads to the south Caribbean, with fly-cruise options from Manchester and stops across Saint Lucia, Grenada, Antigua and beyond. 🌴
Anyone already booked is being contacted directly by MSC, with two clean options: move the booking, or take a full refund. New itineraries open for booking from 25 August 2026.
The nice bit? An agent-booked client doesn't face this alone. You already know the alternatives and can handle the rebooking or refund for them … good news to deliver, not a scramble to manage.

item.title: Got clients eyeing a Mexico cruise? Here's the bit to get right before anything else … under UK pricing rules, the rising port charge has to show up front in the price they see 🌊
item.description:
Got clients eyeing a Mexico cruise? Here's the bit to get right before anything else … under UK pricing rules, the rising port charge has to show up front in the price they see 🌊
As Cruise Trade News reports, Mexico is phasing in a higher cruise passenger tax. It doubled to £7.40 per person on 1 August 2026, rises to £11.10 in July 2027, and reaches £14.80 by August 2028.
The reassuring part? It's charged once per itinerary, not per port call. For a couple, that's roughly £30 in fees by 2028, against about £15 now … which the source calls relatively small in the context of a whole cruise holiday. And with every date published well ahead, there's no scramble.
The helpful bit for agents is transparency: check how each cruise line shows the charge, and make sure it appears up front in line with UK pricing rules. Flag it early, and it's exactly the thoughtful detail that shows clients why an agent is worth having. ✨

item.title: ✈️ Something worth grabbing before the month's out … easyJet holidays is giving travel agents £100 off every booking, and it's trade-only. Clients booking direct won't get near it.
item.description:
✈️ Something worth grabbing before the month's out … easyJet holidays is giving travel agents £100 off every booking, and it's trade-only. Clients booking direct won't get near it.
The way it works is refreshingly simple. Quote the code TRADEEXCLUSIVE on a minimum spend of £1,000 per booking, and the £100 comes off. New bookings only, and the window shuts at 11pm on 1 September 2026.
The nice part? The departure dates run all the way from 19 August 2026 to 31 October 2027, covering beach and city breaks across Europe and North Africa, with the Luxury Collection in the mix too. 💡
easyJet holidays says it's a thank-you to the trade, marking six years of working with agents. Either way, it's a straightforward £100 you can pass to your clients without touching your own pricing.
The deadline's the thing to watch, so worth a look this week.

item.title: Something interesting is happening on the smaller cruise ships this summer... the operators are welcoming a whole new crowd.
item.description:
Something interesting is happening on the smaller cruise ships this summer... the operators are welcoming a whole new crowd.
Unforgettable Croatia says 68% of its summer bookings are first-time cruisers, many of them travellers who'd usually book a boutique hotel on land. Graham Carter sums it up nicely: they see these ships as more like floating luxury hotels.
The appeal is easy to see. Small-ship lines like Windstar, Ponant and HX Expeditions carry fewer than 600 guests... Windstar takes between 148 and 342... so more space, fewer queues, and smaller ports.
And the food does a lot of the talking. 60% of sailors rate food and drink as the best part of a cruise, and Windstar's chef gets a generous budget to shop local markets on port days.
For any client who reckons they've "done cruising", this is a fresh one to put in front of them... a boutique hotel that happens to float.

item.title: The Wave Awards 2026 consumer shortlist is out, and there's a category on it specifically for cruise travel agents. 📣
item.description:
The Wave Awards 2026 consumer shortlist is out, and there's a category on it specifically for cruise travel agents. 📣
World of Cruising surveyed its readers, and the result is 10 public-vote categories, including Favourite Cruise Travel Agent … the booking public celebrating agents right alongside the big cruise lines.
Favourite Ocean Cruise Line alone has 12 nominees, P&O Cruises, Royal Caribbean International and Cunard among them. Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines is headline sponsor, with Marella, Regent Seven Seas and nine other lines backing the night.
Dates to note? Voting closes 30 September, and the ceremony is 24 November at the Dorchester Hotel in London. The early-booking ticket deadline is 30 September too.
If you've clients who love a cruise, send them a quick line before 30 September… a warm reason to reach out, and a lovely reminder that the person planning the holiday matters. 🫶

item.description:
More than a quarter of Fred. Olsen's remaining 2026 sailings are already sold out, and 2027 is running 40% ahead of last year. 🧳

The line has posted its strongest trading day on record, off the back of the 22 July launch of its 87-night 2028 Amazon and Antarctica Grand Voyage… which pulled three times more guests in six days than the 2024 South America launch. Guest numbers overall are up 10% year-on-year.
One more confidence point for you: all three ships… Bolette, Borealis and Balmoral… hit their highest-ever Net Promoter Scores in 2026. Handy reassurance for a first-time cruiser weighing it up. 💡

item.title: 🌍 A little good news for anyone booking holidays for a living this week.
item.description:
🌍 A little good news for anyone booking holidays for a living this week.
Travel agent spend grew again in July, up 2.5% year on year, according to Barclays Consumer Card Spending data reported by Cruise Trade News. That is two months in a row of growth for the agent channel.
What makes it stand out is where it sat. Over the same month, overall travel spend slipped 0.3% and airline spend fell 6.0%… so while parts of the market cooled, the money moving through agents went the other way. Hotels and accommodation had a strong month too, up 2.6%.
Wider UK card spending rose 2.0% in July, its highest level in 12 months, with Barclays noting both essential and non-essential spend stayed in growth 💡
The read? Clients are still booking through people, even when they trim elsewhere. A welcome vote of confidence in what you do.

item.title: 🌍 If you've got clients eyeing a river cruise, point them at the Rhône right now.
item.description:
🌍 If you've got clients eyeing a river cruise, point them at the Rhône right now.
Tauck's Rhône bookings are pacing nearly 30 percent ahead of 2025, and that's before the line's big expansion has even started. The demand is here this season, so it's one to get on with rather than file away.
Behind that demand, Tauck has announced a new Rhône ship, MS Harmonie, built for a quieter, roomier trip. A sister ship to MS Lumière, she carries a maximum of 130 guests… up to 30 percent fewer than comparable riverboats, so the whole ship has a low-density feel. On board there's a swimming pool, a fitness centre, a massage treatment room, a casual dining spot called Arthur's, and generous 300 square foot suites.
She launches in 2028 💡 so flag her for clients planning further ahead. She's one of five new riverboats arriving by 2028, growing Tauck's river capacity by more than 50 percent, with more shoulder-season departures and new six-day formats. Sell the river today, keep Harmonie on the radar for tomorrow.

item.title: Something worth flagging early for anyone booking European travel this summer. 🌍
item.description:
Something worth flagging early for anyone booking European travel this summer. 🌍
You've probably seen the headlines about long queues at EU borders. The new Entry/Exit System, the biometric scheme known as EES, went fully live back in April, and airports have warned of waits up to three hours at peak times, with the busiest hubs edging towards five.
Good news? The Independent reports the EU could delay further post-Brexit border measures to keep travel moving. Schengen countries can partly suspend the checks for up to 90 days to manage the summer crush, so there's a release valve built in.
None of this is set in stone week to week, so it's worth keeping an eye on how individual countries use that window through the summer. For agents, that's a handy bit of context to have ready. A client who has read a scary headline will feel reassured knowing the fuller picture, and you get to be the calm voice while the news shouts. 💡

item.title: Big news in the skies this week … one of Europe's best-known budget airlines is about to get a new owner. ✈️
item.description:
Big news in the skies this week … one of Europe's best-known budget airlines is about to get a new owner. ✈️
The US investment firm Apollo Global Management has agreed a deal to buy easyJet, valuing the airline at around £5.7bn, and the board is recommending it, as Breaking Travel News reports.
Founder Sir Stelios and his family are backing the deal, and a rival bidder has now stepped away. It has been a competitive process, with more than one suitor circling before Apollo came out on top. The deal is not expected to complete until the end of March 2027.
💡 The bit worth knowing? For your clients, nothing changes today. easyJet keeps flying the same routes and honouring every booking, and if anyone asks, their fares and flight times are completely unaffected. One to keep half an eye on as the new owner settles in, not one to worry about.

item.title: 🌍 Spotted a good one for anyone selling cruise this week.
item.description:
🌍 Spotted a good one for anyone selling cruise this week.
Cruise can feel like a lot to pitch, so a few pointers straight from the line itself never go amiss, especially when a client can't decide between a big-ship sailing and something calmer. Princess Cruises took a turn on the Cruise Corner podcast, and its UK sales director Yasmin McKechnie shared her go-to tips for agents.
Her three big ones? Play up the range of ship sizes so there's a fit for every traveller… point to the line's partnerships with global brands as a selling point… and sell the full value, both what's onboard and what's waiting ashore.
She also had a lovely line for client chats, positioning a Princess cruise as "a once in a lifetime experience" 💡
It's a short listen on Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music and YouTube, so you can catch it while the kettle boils. And there's a Princess competition running too, with a Mediterranean cruise for two up for grabs, worth a look while it lasts.

item.title: 🌍 Something worth a look for your cruise clients this morning.
item.description:
🌍 Something worth a look for your cruise clients this morning.
Cruise Trade News has been through the latest World of Cruising search data, and two numbers stand out. The Mediterranean is up around 44% year on year and now pulls nearly half of all cruise searches. The Caribbean has slipped the other way, down about 27%.
People are also booking closer to departure … 52% of exact-month searches are now for sailings within 16 weeks, up from 45% last year.
For you, that means summer and autumn 2026 short-haul is the ready conversation. If a client is thinking "somewhere warm, not too far", the numbers are on your side.
As Raphael Giacardi notes, markets can move fast, so it is worth keeping half an eye on where searches head next.

item.title: Something to keep an eye on if you've got river-cruise clients this summer 🌊
item.description:
Something to keep an eye on if you've got river-cruise clients this summer 🌊
Low water on the Rhine and Danube, after weeks of dry, hot weather, is disrupting some river sailings, and Riviera Travel has moved fast to back its agents through it.
They've set up an incident task force tracking conditions daily, plus a Travel Updates Hub for agents that's refreshed twice a day, so you're not chasing scattered emails for the latest. Call-centre capacity is up, and extra cruise directors and head-office staff have gone onto affected sailings.
Right now 4 of 7 ships are still sailing, 27 departures have run with tailored measures, and 8 have been cancelled. Affected guests get three clear options: a price-matched rebooking, a move to a 2026 or 2027 holiday, or a full refund.
I know a disrupted sailing is never a fun call to take… having it all in one place makes it a good deal easier 💭

item.title: Something new for anyone selling ultra-luxury cruise… 🚢
item.description:
Something new for anyone selling ultra-luxury cruise… 🚢
Explora Journeys, the ultra-luxury line within the MSC Group, is starting to pay travel advisors commission on the shore excursions their clients book. Not only the cabin … the days ashore too. It's being called a first for the ultra-luxury cruise sector.
Explora calls these trips its Destination Experiences, and more than 80% are already booked before guests step aboard. The line wants that closer to 90%, and reckons advisors are the ones to help get it there.
Justin Poulsen, who heads Destination Experiences at Explora, called it "brilliant news for the travel advisor community" … and it's hard to argue. You're already matching clients to the right day ashore. Now that care shows up in your commission too. 💭
Worth getting to know the Destination Experiences catalogue soon … so you've got answers ready when the next luxury-cruise enquiry comes your way, not scrambling to catch up.

item.title: Now here's a lovely one to start your Tuesday. 🌍
item.description:
Now here's a lovely one to start your Tuesday. 🌍
Carly Taylor-Davis had been in the industry less than a year when she was handed a customer who had already walked away from two colleagues. Not the easiest start… but Carly stuck with it.
Her secret? Patience, plain and simple. "I was just comfortable with her. I had patience because some people need that," she told TTG Media.
That patience turned a wary customer, Joyce, into one of Seaside Travel's most loyal cruise clients. She now books her Fred Olsen sailings through Carly alone… and will even ring mid-cruise to extend a trip and let Carly sort the rest. 💭
It's a warm reminder that the win isn't always in the offer. Sometimes it's in slowing down and giving someone time to trust you. ✨
Worth a thought for anyone on your own books who's gone quiet… a gentle check-in might be all it takes.
Cheering Carly on from here.

item.title: If you've got clients heading to Crete, this one's worth a quick read. Wildfires on the island have forced evacuations affecting around 8,000 residents and tourists, and as of 31 July 2026 it's still a developing situation, not a resolved one. 💭
item.description:
If you've got clients heading to Crete, this one's worth a quick read. Wildfires on the island have forced evacuations affecting around 8,000 residents and tourists, and as of 31 July 2026 it's still a developing situation, not a resolved one. 💭
The UK advice is calm and clear: stay in touch with your travel provider, follow local safety instructions, and don't rush to cancel.
Here's the part where you come in. Which? Travel's Rory Boland warns that "travellers who cancel now will likely forfeit the right to a refund or rebooking." So a panicked cancellation can cost your client their protection.
For a JLT client, their travel provider is you. You're their line to the booking, the supplier, and their real options … the steady voice when they're worried.
Greek Tourism Minister Olga Kefalogianni says "the safety of residents and visitors remains our absolute priority," with response efforts ongoing.

item.title: Something worth knowing about this summer's heatwave chaos... 🌍
item.description:
Something worth knowing about this summer's heatwave chaos... 🌍
As the heat swept across Europe and travel plans wobbled, new data analysed by 247 Travel Partner Desk (247tpd) looked at who fixes things best when disruption hits. The answer? Real, human travel agents.
Specialist human support reached resolution quality of up to 90%, and 100% in some cases. AI-only support came in at 69%. That's roughly a 30% edge for people over the bots when a trip goes sideways. 💡
These are 247tpd's figures, from a firm that works only in travel support... but they line up with something plenty of us already sense. When a holiday gets messy, a knowledgeable human who can see the whole picture beats a chatbot cycling you through menus.
So if you've clients heading into the heat, it's worth a quick look at their booking now... what's flexible, what can move, and making sure they've got you on hand rather than an app queue if a flight or transfer wobbles.
Good news for anyone who books with a real agent.

~ The JLT Daily Despatch with Sophie Skies, Your Daily Travel News Scout

item.title: Here's a handy one to tuck away for your winter conversations. Aviation analyst John Strickland, who heads JLS Consulting, reckons high fuel costs could see European and US airlines ground more aircraft than usual this winter, with the weaker, marginal routes the ones most likely to feel it.
item.description:
Here's a handy one to tuck away for your winter conversations. Aviation analyst John Strickland, who heads JLS Consulting, reckons high fuel costs could see European and US airlines ground more aircraft than usual this winter, with the weaker, marginal routes the ones most likely to feel it.
This is his professional forecast, not a confirmed schedule change. Strickland shared it at a World Aviation Festival webinar on 16 July 2026.
The useful bit is the split. The routes in the frame are the quieter city pairs and thin, off-peak services that only ever half-filled. The big winter-sun corridors are barely exposed … demand keeps those seats selling whatever fuel does.
So it's worth a quick sort of your winter bookings. A client on a mainstream sun route needs no nudge. A client on a quieter city pair or a less-travelled airport is the one to have a word with, because those are the routes that could tighten first. Book that group early and they keep the most choice on price and timings.
Full blog on the website 👇 link in the first comment
~ The JLT Daily Despatch with Sophie Skies, Your Daily Travel News Scout

item.title: Got clients who have sailed with Cunard before? This one's for them. ✨
item.description:
Got clients who have sailed with Cunard before? This one's for them. ✨
Cunard has opened an exclusive 10% saving for returning guests on selected 2027 and 2028 voyages. The catch is the booking window… it runs from 23 July to 31 August 2026, so it's worth a quick call to your Cunard loyalists.
It applies to a Cunard Fare or Early Saver Fare voyage of 7 to 67 nights, departing between January 2027 and March 2028. 🗓️ Plenty of scope, then, whether they fancy a week away or something longer.
There's a bigger story too. In 2027, three Queens ships sail UK roundtrips for the first time since 2018, pushing Southampton capacity up 54%. That means more sailings, more choice, and White Star service on every one of them. ✈️
If you know a couple who cruised with Cunard last year, or a returning solo guest who loved life aboard, this is a lovely reason to check in before the window closes. A saving for their past custom, plus first pick of the new roundtrip sailings from Southampton.

item.title: Around 2.2 million of us are heading abroad this bank holiday, and for a lot of your clients it'll be their first meet-and-greet with EES at the border. ✈️
item.description:
Around 2.2 million of us are heading abroad this bank holiday, and for a lot of your clients it'll be their first meet-and-greet with EES at the border. ✈️
EES has been in full force since April, so passport control into Europe can take a little longer than last summer... photo and fingerprints on arrival now. Spain's the big pick this weekend, with Greece, Portugal, Italy and Turkey close behind.
ABTA's advice is simple enough to pass straight on to clients... leave plenty of time for the journey, because for many travellers this is their first run-in with EES and passport control may take longer than usual.
Your steadying line? Arrive early, build in a buffer, documents ready. 💡 One handy note for Greek island bookings... Greece has said it won't add the extra biometric checks for UK nationals.
Nothing here changes the holiday waiting on the other side. A short pre-departure message from you does most of the reassuring.

~ The JLT Daily Despatch with Sophie Skies, Your Daily Travel News Scout

item.title: Cunard fans, this one's for the diary. 🌊
item.description:
Cunard fans, this one's for the diary. 🌊
Queen Victoria is heading into dry dock this autumn for a proper refresh, and she's back in service on 7 November with some lovely new touches.
The Grand Lobby and Queens Room are being refreshed, the Queens Grill and Princess Grill Suites reimagined, and there's a new Pavilion Wellness Café built around a plant-based, sustainable menu.
The bit worth flagging? Eight new Britannia staterooms, three of them in a brand-new Britannia Deluxe Oceanview category with floor-to-ceiling windows.
Sales opened on 20 July for voyages from 11 November, and she is already showing up on the booking systems. With the Mediterranean, Norwegian Fjords, and Canary Islands all on her 2027 map, there's a natural reason to check in with your Cunard regulars.

item.title: Morning, all… a practical one for anyone with clients flying home from Europe this summer. ✈️
item.description:
Morning, all… a practical one for anyone with clients flying home from Europe this summer. ✈️
The EU's new entry-exit system, the EES, has nearly tripled passport-control times for Brits at some airports. At Rome's Fiumicino, the wait has gone from 7 minutes to 20, according to the airport's chief aviation officer.
The system asks UK travellers for a fingerprint and photo on entry to the Schengen area, and that first-time step is where the queues have grown. 💡
Here's the useful bit for your clients: Wizz Air UK now says to arrive three hours before the flight home, up from two, and to pack a portable charger and some water for the queue.
It's not the same everywhere. France reports no major congestion at its hubs, and biometric e-gate kiosks are helping elsewhere. A quick heads-up before your clients travel goes a long way.

item.title: Qantas has just confirmed Sydney to London as the first Project Sunrise route, with the non-stop service launching October 2027.
item.description:
Qantas has just confirmed Sydney to London as the first Project Sunrise route, with the non-stop service launching October 2027.
It ends almost 80 years of stopovers on the Kangaroo Route. Back in 1947, the same journey took four days and seven stops… now it’s 22 hours, one flight, no transit.
The aircraft is a custom Airbus A350-1000ULR with an extra 20,000-litre fuel tank, and Qantas has ordered 12 of them. Tickets are expected on sale February 2027, so there’s plenty of runway to build the knowledge before your clients start asking.
Worth holding onto: the existing Perth-London and Sydney-Singapore-London services aren’t going anywhere, and Sydney-New York is confirmed as the next Sunrise route. So if you’ve got a client weighing up Australia for 2027 or 2028, you’ve now got three different shapes of the same trip to talk through.
